organization: CERN, in collaboration with DESY (Hamburg) and the ELSA accelerator (University of Bonn)
secondary_character: genuine research — teams design and then actually run a particle-physics experiment on a real beamline
cycle_evidence: 2026 cycle closed. FAQ: proposals could be submitted between 'January 2026 and the deadline: 13 March 2026 at 23:59 CEST'; winners notified in June, invited at the end of August. No 2027 cycle dates published as of retrieval.
age_rule_verbatim: 'For participation in the competition, there is no age limit. Students under the age of 16 can be members of a team. They can participate anonymously or with parental consent... The main limitation for students younger than 16 years is that if their team wins, only students who are at least 16 years old on the first day of their stay at CERN, DESY or ELSA can travel.'
age_rule_note: Two-tier and must not be flattened to a single minimum_age: no age floor to COMPETE, but 16+ on the first day of the stay to TRAVEL if the team wins. Storing minimum_age=16 would wrongly exclude a 15-year-old who can legitimately enter.
eligibility_verbatim: 'Students from all over the world are eligible to participate in BL4S.'
eligibility_placement: Answer to the FAQ question 'Who is eligible to submit an experiment proposal?' — i.e. inside the eligibility answer itself, not a marketing banner. Meets the placement test.
team_rule_verbatim: 'A team needs to consist of a minimum of 5 members'; 'A maximum of 9 students per winning team will be invited to CERN, DESY or ELSA.'
cost_verbatim: 'There are no fees or anything similar; taking part is completely free. For the winning teams, BL4S will cover the full costs of the winners' participation in the competition, including travel, accommodation and three meals per day.'
coach_rule_verbatim: 'The team coach needs to be an adult. Very often, this person is a teacher at the students' school, but this is not mandatory. The coach can be a mentor from another institution or even a parent or student at the university.'
selectivity: Proposals evaluated by experts; a small number of winning teams travel to run their experiment. Landing page states proposals have come from 89 different countries. Exact acceptance rate NOT STATED on official pages.
why_high_value: Free, genuinely worldwide, team-based, and the output is real experimental physics on a CERN/DESY beamline — one of very few opportunities at this level with no cost barrier at all. Directly addresses ORYN's research-exposure gap for 14-18.
unresolved: 2027 cycle dates unpublished — must be re-checked in January 2027 rather than inferred.
No official acceptance rate published; selectivity should be described qualitatively, not numerically.

canonical_name: TÜBİTAK 2204-A Lise Öğrencileri Araştırma Projeleri Yarışması (High School Students Research Projects Competition)
organization: TÜBİTAK — Bilim İnsanı Destek Programları Başkanlığı (BİDEB)
secondary_character: genuine research — entries must be COMPLETED original research projects, not ideas
cycle_evidence: Call document §3: 'Yarışma için yılda bir kez başvuru alınır. Çağrı açılış ve kapanış tarihleri, Bölge ve final aşamalarının düzenlenme tarihleri, yarışmanın web sayfasında ilan edilir.' — i.e. once per year, dates published separately on the competition web page. This is an explicit official 'announced elsewhere', NOT a rolling intake.
last_cycle_note: 2026 call (2025-26 academic year) ran 2025-10-13 to 2025-12-12 17:30 per TÜBİTAK announcement surfaced in search; the call PDF itself carries no dates. Next cycle would be expected to open around October 2026 — MUST be re-checked, not inferred.
age_rule_verbatim: 4.1.6 'Yarışmaya başvuracak öğrenciler, yarışma başvuru tarihinin son günü itibarıyla 20 yaşından gün almamış olmalıdır.'
age_rule_note: Must not have turned 20 as of the final application day. maximum_age=19 encodes this; the real rule is date-relative to the closing date.
eligibility_verbatim: 4.1.1 'Yarışmaya, Türkiye ve KKTC'de örgün ve açık öğretim sisteminde öğrenim gören tüm lise öğrencileri katılabilir.'
eligibility_note: Explicitly includes açık öğretim (open/distance education) students, not just örgün (formal schooling) — a real inclusion that matters and is easy to lose in paraphrase. Criterion is WHERE YOU STUDY, not citizenship: a foreign national enrolled in a Turkish high school qualifies; a Turkish citizen studying abroad does not.
team_rule_verbatim: 4.1.2 'Yarışmaya her öğrenci yalnızca bir proje ile katılabilir ve her proje en çok üç öğrenci tarafından hazırlanır.'
advisor_rule_verbatim: 4.1.3 'Bir projede sadece bir danışman görev alabilir... Projede danışman olması zorunlu değildir.'
exclusivity_rule_verbatim: 4.1.9 — a project found to have been submitted to ANY other project competition (same or similar content, same or different name) before this competition's closing date is disqualified at whatever stage it has reached. Also 4.1.8: projects submitted in previous years cannot be re-entered.
exclusivity_note: DECISION-CRITICAL and easy to miss: a Turkish student cannot enter the same project into 2204-A and another competition in the same window. This constrains sequencing, so the advisor must surface it BEFORE a student double-submits.
completeness_rule_verbatim: 4.1.7 'Fikir aşamasında veya devam etmekte olan projelerle yarışmaya başvuru yapılmaz.' — idea-stage or in-progress projects are rejected.
cost_verbatim: No fee appears anywhere in the 17-page call document. §2.1.2: travel, accommodation and meal costs of students invited to the regional and final stages — plus one advisor or guide teacher per project — are covered by TÜBİTAK.
stages: Regional (Bölge) exhibition -> regional 1st places advance to the national Final. §2.2.2-2.2.4: cash prizes and certificates at both stages; §2.2.5 patent registration support for national top-three.
university_admission_benefit: HIGHEST-VALUE FIELD. §7.1.1: national 1st/2nd/3rd place winners, and students sent by TÜBİTAK to international project competitions who place top-three there, receive an 'Ek Katsayı' (extra coefficient) on the YKS university entrance exam — once only, in their first exam year, if they choose a department related to their winning field. §7.1.2: students sent by TÜBİTAK to international competitions who place top-three are placed into a related higher-education programme by ÖSYM 'sınavsız' — WITHOUT the entrance exam. Both require a separate application to TÜBİTAK within the window in the current YKS guide; tracking that is the student's own responsibility.
fetch_method: WebFetch + local pypdf text extraction (WebFetch could not parse the PDF)
why_high_value: For a student in Türkiye this is plausibly the single highest-value record in the whole corpus: free, pays travel, is genuine research, and its top prizes convert directly into university admission advantage (extra coefficient, or exam-free placement via international placement). ORYN currently has no TÜBİTAK competition at all.
unresolved: 2027 cycle dates unpublished as of retrieval — re-check the competition web page around October 2026.
Prize amounts are published on the competition web page, not in the call document — not yet retrieved.

canonical_name: Regeneron International Science and Engineering Fair (Regeneron ISEF)
secondary_character: genuine research — the world's largest pre-college science research competition
cycle_evidence: 'May 9-15, 2027, Phoenix Convention Center, Phoenix, Arizona' stated on the official ISEF page.
event_location: Phoenix Convention Center, Phoenix, Arizona, USA
deadline_note: There is NO central ISEF application deadline. Entry is exclusively by winning at an ISEF-affiliated local/regional/state/national fair, and each affiliated fair sets its own timeline. Storing a single deadline here would be fabrication; the actionable date is the student's own affiliated fair's, found via findafair.societyforscience.org.
age_rule_verbatim: 'not have reached age 20 on or before May 1 preceding ISEF'
grade_rule_note: 'or equivalent' is what makes this workable for non-US school systems.
eligibility_verbatim: 'The finalists, selected from 365 affiliate fairs in more than 60 countries, regions, and territories... earned the right to compete at the Regeneron International Science and Engineering Fair by winning at a Society-affiliated local, regional, state, or national science fair.' Rules page: 'All domestic and international students competing in an ISEF-affiliated fair must adhere to all rules'.
eligibility_note: NOT open-entry worldwide. Eligibility is conditional on an affiliated fair existing in the student's country/region. 'More than 60 countries' is stated but the official page gives no country list, so per-country eligibility must be checked through findafair, never assumed.
team_rule_verbatim: 'Teams must have no more than three members'
project_rule_verbatim: 'Each student is only allowed to enter one project. That project may include no more than 12 months of continuous research'
cost_note: NOT STATED on official pages. Affiliated-fair entry costs vary by fair and are set by the fair, not by Society for Science. Must not be recorded as free.
selectivity: Roughly 1,600-1,900 finalists drawn from an estimated millions of students competing in the affiliated-fair pyramid; official pages state 365 affiliate fairs in 60+ countries but publish no acceptance rate. Describe qualitatively.
why_high_value: The most recognised pre-college research competition in the world and entirely absent from the corpus. Critically, its true actionable step for a student is 'find and enter your affiliated fair', which is a different and much earlier action than 'apply to ISEF' — exactly the kind of thing the advisor must get right.
unresolved: No official per-country affiliated-fair list retrieved; needs a findafair lookup per student country before telling any specific student they are eligible.
Cost to the student at the affiliated-fair level is fair-specific and unretrieved.
